raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies the intended course set in 32/40 exports, below the 95% target; overall median handling is 17 minutes. Unchanged-assignment centers achieve seven minutes, suggesting useful existing behavior, without establishing causality. Six affected exports coincide with assignment changes. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation: missing records and failed name matching remain distinguishable possibilities. Fast execution and slow replacements suggest delivery delay, but waiting is not necessarily handling. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish safety for the unsampled split-course center.

openings.claim: Current-assignment selection may omit courses for historical weeks; separately, renaming may make present courses appear absent during coordinator comparison.
openings.delta: Distinguish incorrect membership from recognition errors before changing export selection or labels.
openings.prediction: With an agreed intended set held fixed, assignment changes alter exported membership if the first mechanism holds; renaming preserves membership but disrupts coordinator matching if the second holds.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split courses for one requested week. Compare internal course identities and exported rows with coordinator-agreed expectations; include another center as an isolation check. Retain the documented CSV schema and concurrent attendance entry. Time-box diagnosis within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Staging can reproduce assignment and naming transitions.
Agreement on intended courses can be established independently of current export output.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling arise mainly from reconciling course expectations, or from downloading and spreadsheet import?
openings.delta: Separates an unobserved workflow bottleneck from execution and replacement waiting time.
openings.prediction: If reconciliation dominates, active checking and correction expand on disputed-course files while download/import times remain similar; an import bottleneck produces a different allocation.
openings.probe: Use six coordinators’ two short sessions with fabricated ordinary and disputed-course CSVs, counterbalancing order. Time checking, correction, download and import separately; record passive waiting separately. Run within the same six-day budget using authorized workspaces without interrupting attendance entry.
assumptions: Fabricated files approximate ordinary spreadsheet workflows.
Session results guide a bounded change; they do not establish the next-40-export success measures.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renames coincide with most affected exports, but causation and handling-time components are unmeasured. These combinations are hypotheses. The clean sample does not establish isolation for split courses or future exports.

openings.claim: Combine week-aware course identity resolution with coordinator confirmation of the intended course set at a center/week manifest interface. Resolve selected stable identifiers to the requested week's course relationships before producing the documented CSV.
openings.delta: Historical resolution alone may reproduce an unintended schedule; confirmation alone may select labels that resolve incorrectly after renames or reassignment. Their interaction could align coordinator intent with exported membership.
openings.prediction: The combination reduces intended-set errors on changed-course fixtures more than either component alone, without confirmation effort erasing the handling-time gain.
openings.probe: Counterbalance baseline, resolver-only, confirmation-only and combined workflows across fabricated reassignment, rename and split fixtures with six coordinators. Independently specify expected course sets; record total handling time and every exported row's center. Keep confirmation private and preserve CSV schema. Reject implementation exceeding six engineer-days or hosting allowance; test simultaneous attendance entry.
assumptions: Stable course identity and sufficient historical relationships are available or recoverable within budget.
Coordinators can identify intended sets despite incomplete timetables.
Selection and row retrieval both enforce authorized center scope.

openings.claim: Combine coordinator-triggered replacement with revision-bound export receipts at the generation/download interface: each private receipt identifies center, week, course set and captured attendance revision, and flags subsequent relevant changes.
openings.delta: On-demand regeneration alone can repeatedly deliver stale files; revision visibility alone leaves replacement delays. Together they could enable an informed, immediate replacement while instructors continue editing.
openings.prediction: Under controlled concurrent edits, the combination reduces stale-file acceptance relative to on-demand alone and repair delay relative to receipts alone.
openings.probe: Compare those three variants using fabricated attendance edits before, during and after generation; measure repair delay, stale acceptance, workload and write latency. Put receipts outside the unchanged CSV. Verify authorized-center rows throughout.
assumptions: Existing storage supports consistent nonblocking reads and cheap relevant revision tracking within six engineer-days and hosting allowance.
Coordinators understand revision notices; this mechanism alone does not repair incorrect course selection.

openings.claim: Historical assignments may omit courses; renames may obscure present courses. Combine week-aware identity resolution with intended-set confirmation.
openings.discriminator: Omission versus recognition; resolver alone may preserve wrong intent, confirmation alone misresolve changed labels.
openings.probe: Counterbalance baseline/resolver/confirmation/combined on unchanged/reassigned/renamed/split fixtures. Compare identities/rows against independent agreed sets; measure handling and cross-center rows.
openings.uncertainty: Reproducible transitions, sufficient timetables, affordable historical identity recovery and center-scoped selection/retrieval unverified.

openings.claim: Reconciliation or download/import may dominate handling.
openings.probe: Counterbalance ordinary/disputed fabricated CSVs; time each activity.

openings.claim: On-demand replacement plus revision receipts may reduce stale acceptance and repair delay.
openings.discriminator: Regeneration alone risks staleness; receipts alone retain delay.
openings.probe: Compare combined/regeneration/receipts with edits before/during/after generation; measure staleness, delay, workload, write latency and authorized rows.
openings.uncertainty: Affordable nonblocking consistent reads/revision tracking and understandable notices unproven; incorrect selection remains.

lineage.reason: With Z1; preserves interaction and component comparisons.

post_distill.decision: Diagnose first. Use private fabricated staging/authorized workspaces, documented CSV, concurrent attendance entry, six coordinators/two short sessions, shared six-engineer-day/hosting limit. Receipts outside CSV identify center/week/course set/captured revision and flag relevant changes. Associations establish no causality; sampled isolation excludes split-course evidence. Sessions cannot establish next-40 targets: median ≤12 minutes, ≥95% intended sets, zero cross-center rows.
